title: Ghost/spawn pivot must be the block's geometric centre, not the origin cell
description: Owner 2026-09-20: 'the part of the block that the cursor attaches to must always be the center of the block, otherwise it's impossible to stack off-centered blocks'. BlockShape.cells are offsets from the origin cell, so shapes whose centroid is not the origin (bars, L, T, dominoes) hang off the cursor and rotate about the wrong point. Fix: compute the shape's cell-bounds centre (BlockShape.center() -> Vector3, cached) and offset both the ghost mesh (GhostPreview) and the spawned body (BlockFactory/Match._spawn_block, and the client copy in MatchNet.net_block_spawned) so the cursor/hit point is the centre of the block and all rotations are about it. Preview/validity raycast (Territory v2 B) uses the same centre. Tests: for every shape in config/blocks, the ghost's AABB centre equals the cursor point (within cube_size/2 on Y), and the spawned block's AABB centre matches the ghost's.

title: M3b review fixes: Steam lobby leak on failed client peer, double host_online/join_lobby while pending, burn-clamp escape margin
description: stackfall-reviewer findings on the P1 candidate (orchestrator-verified by source). (1) Net._on_steam_lobby_joined: when response==1 but _make_steam_client_peer returns null, _fail_join->leave() never calls steam_provider.leave_lobby (lobby id not yet stored) -> orphaned Steam membership; host path already leaves. Fix + assert fake.leave_lobby_calls. (2) host_online()/join_lobby() have no in-flight guard: a second call while the first create_lobby/join_lobby is pending issues a second request; the late callback is dropped by the _mode guard -> orphaned Steam lobby. Fix with a pending token/flag (refuse or leave the stale lobby) + regression test. (3) Match._clamp_disk_origin_for_burn margin 0.9 leaves only field_radius of slack, but _burn_block's outward impulse (30 on mass 1, 0.35 up) travels ~95 m horizontally before reaching kill_plane_y=-40 -> a max-clamped hostile burn exits the kill-plane box footprint and falls forever. Orchestrator numbers: v~22 m/s horizontal, t~4.3 s. Fix: clamp to field_radius*KILL_PLANE_RADIUS_FACTOR*0.5*0.5 (slack >=150 m on the small map) and add a physics-stepping test asserting Events.block_removed fires for a maximally clamped outward burn. Dispatch after P3 (single writer in M:/Bontago).

Orchestrator read-only diagnostic at 081ae21 (no runtime repro yet; no files edited). Two distinct defects confirmed by source:
(1) First network start: Match.start_match() calls _set_state(LOADING) (Match.gd:166) BEFORE _build_territory() (:171). Next host/join -> _show_lobby -> register_world -> start_match emits (PLAYING->LOADING); Main only rebuilds on from==LOBBY (:179), so the second match has no world (no HotSeat/PlayerController/SnapshotSync). Reachable today: client whose host quit then hosts again. No UI leave/rematch button exists yet (grep ui/*.gd: none).

title: Single-cell hole does not swallow a block

This deviates from spec 2.2 ('blocks resting on holes fall through' has no carve-out for a single cell). There is a deliberately pending test that documents the exact failure: tests/unit/test_field_cells.gd::test_a_block_over_a_lone_hole_cell_falls_through (currently marked pending() because it fails). The proper fix is a rebuildable trimesh top surface for the disk instead of one BoxShape3D per cell -- a P3-sized geometry redesign per docs/M2_PLAN.md's Known limitations section, not a quick fix-pass change. Narrowing cell_overlap back down regresses tests/bench/bench_tower (cell_overlap is load-bearing for tower stability), so the fix must preserve tower stability while still letting a lone hole swallow a block.

The plan implemented option (b) -- a NetConfig.disconnect_grace = 10 s grace period, then the slot is eliminated exactly as a lost home flag does it (Events.player_eliminated) via Match.on_peer_left(slot_id) -- rather than (a) towers stay forever or (c) AI takeover (needs M5). Shipped without an explicit owner sign-off.

title: Verify gamepad feel on real hardware
description: Gamepad support (ghost movement, rotation, camera orbit/pan/zoom, placement, menu navigation) is only tested headlessly via synthetic InputEventJoypad* events through Input.parse_input_event (per CLAUDE.md's approach for hardware that can't be used in automated tests). Real analog stick feel, deadzones, and trigger behavior with a physical gamepad are unverified.

Report any dead zones, drift, or feel issues; re-verify after M3a/M4 add net-debug-toggle and special-throw bindings.

title: Verify LAN discovery across two physical machines
description: M3a's LAN discovery (net/LanDiscovery.gd, UDP broadcast advertising) and ENet hosting/joining have only been exercised on one machine via direct-IP loopback and the local multi-instance harness (tools/run_m3a_local.ps1/.sh), because PacketPeerUDP.bind() sets no SO_REUSEADDR and only one process per PC can listen on port 47777 (docs/M3a_PLAN.md's Known limitations). Real two-machine LAN discovery and play is unverified and needs the owner's hardware.
acceptance_criteria: Manual steps for the owner: (1) run the game on two PCs on the same LAN; (2) on PC A, Host a match from the main menu; (3) on PC B, open Join and confirm PC A's game appears in the LAN list within a few seconds (discovery_broadcast_hz=1); (4) join it and confirm both PCs see each other's blocks and territory in real time; (5) as a fallback, confirm direct-IP join (PC B enters PC A's LAN IP:47778) also works. Report ping_ms and any hitches back to the project.

title: Territory solve cost above the graded size
description: Per config/TerritoryTuning.gd's measured table, TerritorySolver's solve cost is roughly 20 ms for 400 circles and roughly 30 ms for 600 circles at the 10 Hz solve rate -- above the per-solve budget once circle count climbs. max_circles = 400 currently caps it in the resource (never in code, per CLAUDE.md's no-magic-numbers rule). The next optimisation identified is incremental raster re-stamping (only re-stamp circles that changed) instead of re-stamping every circle every tick.
acceptance_criteria: Either document that max_circles=400 is an acceptable permanent cap for supported player/map-size combinations, or implement incremental raster re-stamping and show bench_territory meeting the 8 ms/solve budget at a higher circle count.

title: bench_rain headroom shrank after velocity_steps increase
description: Jolt velocity_steps was raised to 192 (needed for tower stability), which took tests/bench/bench_rain's 300-block worst case from roughly 2.8 ms to roughly 5 ms against spec 3.5's 8.33 ms per-frame budget at 60 Hz. Still passing, but headroom is much thinner. Re-check bench_rain timing when M4's specials add more bodies to the world (gift crates, thrown specials, orbs, etc.), and again when M8's stable-block freezing lands (freezing bodies changes the physics solver's workload).
acceptance_criteria: bench_rain re-measured after M4 lands specials and again after M8 lands stable-block freezing; if either regresses toward or past the 8.33 ms budget, tune Jolt/PhysicsTuning settings (in the resource, never as literals in code) rather than removing velocity_steps=192, since that was needed for tower stability.

comments.author: Tony
comments.text:
Re-measured on an idle machine (2026-09-18) to settle a false regression alarm from the M3a integration pass, which reported ~15.5 ms (64.7 fps, FAIL). That number was contaminated by concurrent Claude agents/Godot instances running on the same machine during that session -- a stray headless bench_territory process (PID 11964/11640, started 08:11, hung at 0% CPU) was also found and reported, though it was not itself consuming CPU by the time of this test.

Verified idle-machine numbers at main (b0314c7), 5 runs of tests/bench/bench_rain.tscn:
  5.5153, 4.9344, 5.4041, 5.1882, 5.0001 ms -- mean ~5.21 ms, all PASS (target 8.3333 ms).

Comparison at the M2 commit (3e48be2), via a disposable git worktree with a fresh --import (no parse error this time -- the M3a integrator's worktree issue didn't reproduce), 5 runs:
  10.3621 (first-run warm-up outlier), 5.7137, 4.6066, 5.2771, 4.7804 ms -- settled mean ~5.09 ms.

main and M2 perform equivalently within noise (~4.6-5.7 ms sustained, matching this issue's "roughly 5 ms" estimate). Confirmed by code audit that bench_rain.tscn has no functional dependency on Net/Match/SnapshotSync/MatchNet: none of those autoloads define _physics_process, Match/Net's _process bodies are no-ops or cheap when offline, and Main.gd (the only place that calls SnapshotSync.host_tick/client_tick) is not part of the bench_rain scene. BlockRegistry is likewise only a child of Main, not instantiated by bench_rain's Field. Verdict: measurement contamination, not a regression. No code change made. Headroom is still thin per this issue's existing concern (roughly 40% under budget) -- the M4/M8 re-check plan here still stands.

title: Net Steam session: cancel-and-retry before Steam answers can misattribute the late lobby callback
description: After mv0.2.6: host_online() -> leave() -> host_online() all before the first create_lobby answers: the first attempt's late lobby_created is consumed as the second attempt's answer (single _steam_request_pending flag; GodotSteam lobby_created/lobby_joined carry no per-call id). The second attempt's real answer is then abandoned as stale. Narrow UI race (needs the menu to allow re-hosting while pending, which ERR_BUSY currently prevents unless leave() is called in between). Fix idea: generation counter captured at call time + compare in callbacks; leave any lobby whose generation is stale.
